what_this_is: The registry of every run the pre-analysis plan lists on outcomes, in its order of unblinding, with each run's plan section, sets, design builder, estimator, labels and status. A list only: no design is built for it and no outcome, price, revenue or bill is read. The plan was frozen on Joe's explicit approval on 2026-11-20 at commit ea426c4 (approved specification ed3a2ff); it is internally frozen and not externally preregistered. When this registry was last brought to the code, on 2026-11-20 (session 27), the gate file GATE1_SIGNED did not exist and access to outcomes had not been authorized. A status of 'built' means the builder and the estimator compose on invented inputs (tests/test_run_outcomes_invented.py), nothing more. Row M is out of scope for this freeze by Joe's ruling of 2026-11-19 (D-109) and is listed after the executable order of unblinding, not in it.

statuses.built: design builder and estimator exist and compose on invented inputs
statuses.design_only: a builder exists; what is missing is named
statuses.needs_package: the pinned package is not installed
statuses.blocked: the run is defined and something named stops it
statuses.not_built: the plan lists the run and no module covers it
statuses.out_of_scope_for_this_freeze: out of scope for this freeze by Joe's ruling of 2026-11-19 (D-109): not run, in no executable order of unblinding and in no built count; its code is dormant

outcome_access: load_outcomes_after_the_freeze is the only door to outcomes. It refuses in words a purpose other than 'outcome_analysis_after_the_freeze' (panel.load_outcomes' exempt purposes, construction QA and the power simulation, are never taken through it), then refuses unless GATE1_SIGNED exists, then unless DCUB_OUTCOME_RUN_AUTHORIZED=1, then unless PREANALYSIS.md is committed with no uncommitted change and the freeze commit ea426c4 is an ancestor of HEAD, and it refuses power_simulation.read_listed_outcomes as a reader. Only then does it call the reader, panel.load_outcomes by default, once, with purpose='outcome_analysis_after_the_freeze' and nothing else, and it returns the frame untouched with a record of how it was read that carries no outcome value. The gate file is created only on Joe's separate authorization to access outcomes. No other path in this module loads outcomes, and every runner takes its outcome frame as an argument.
order_of_unblinding_means: the executable order: every entry but those out of scope for this freeze, in the plan's order; run_all runs these and no other
built_is_not_ready: 'built' means the builder and the estimator compose on invented inputs, nothing more. A built entry with a non-empty needs_before_research_data still needs those inputs from the caller before it can run on research data. They are inputs built by named functions from named files under rules the plan and Joe's rulings state, row C's fiber shares (December filings, D-107) among them. No needs text of a built entry names an element as the caller's choice; the last one so named, which history of the inventory is supplied to inventory_against_sales, was settled by Joe on 2026-11-20 (D-119) as the inventory as built, the load history underlying the headline design, which the registry supplies as RunInputs.side.dose. Some needs carry a condition that cannot be checked before outcomes are read (whether row U's flags frame covers every outcome unit-year) or before a check passes (the per-state reconstruction check, before a scenario's work is used in that state), and row U's flags over step U3's window rest on the session's reading of that window, which Joe may strike.
stopped_steps_means: a built entry composes on invented inputs; a step listed in its stopped_on_research_inputs cannot run on the real quantity files until Joe rules or authorizes what it names

Step U3's window is 2015 to 2025, so the flags are built with step_window=(2015, 2025), the adopted rule applied year by year over the step's own window; one frame of 2015 to 2025 built that way serves every step, since a filing counts for its own year alone (the session's reading, which Joe may strike). On the records no 2025 unit-year of the quantity panel has a filer-table row (1,362 unit-years, 0 with a record of a filing; data/frozen/reconciliation_mu_design.json). An outcome unit-year the frame does not cover stops the step in words and it is recorded as not computed; whether the frame covers every outcome unit-year cannot be shown before outcomes are read. Short Form exclusion as adopted by Joe on 2026-11-20 (D-115): a utility-state-year leaves where a record shows a Short Form filing, a row in the Short Form table that year or, for 2019, a flag of true in the operational file. Every other unit-year is kept with no record of a filing, which is no claim about whether it filed. The three-year count is taken after the exclusion. The 2019 exclusion is explicitly incomplete. The table has no 2019 rows, the exclusion that year rests on the operational file's flags, and a 2019 unit-year with a missing flag or with no flags row is kept with no record either way. A missing flag or an absent row does not establish non-filing. The sample is still not the paper's sample, and the row is comparison-only (D-109). Outcome availability (whether a unit-year has a price) is not used in place of the paper's Short Form exclusion (Joe, 2026-11-19, D-109). On the quantity side (data/frozen/reconciliation_mu_design.json, short_form_flags_for_row_u), the frame with no exclusion has 16,648 unit-years and 1,808 utilities; one flagged unit-year of 2019 leaves directly, and the same utility's 2023 and 2024 leave through the three-year requirement, leaving 16,645 unit-years and 1,807 utilities. Of the frame's 1,974 unit-years of 2019, 1 has a flag of true, 1,780 have a missing flag and 193 have no flags row, the last two kept with no record either way. The filer table has rows in each year from 2012 to 2018 and from 2020 to 2025 and none in 2019; of its 13,090 unit-years in row U's window of 2015 to 2024, none has a row in the quantity panel (data/interim/panel_quantities.parquet). No price is read for these counts, so the paper's missing-price drop is not applied and this is not the paper's sample. The paper's 1,798 utilities retained and its Short Form group of approximately 560 are printed beside ours for comparison only and are no part of any reason. U0's treatment is cumulative_mw on reconciliation_treatment.assign_polygon_smallest(sites, data/interim/reconciliation_polygon_incidence.parquet, data/interim/panel_reported_ids.parquet, **ROW_U_POLYGON), the smallest containing polygon over every polygon with the type not read, our labelled approximation (D-109), built on the real quantity files 2026-11-19 (2,157 of 2,203 data center sites mapped to a panel unit; one exact area tie listed, not broken; that site has no assigned polygon, is listed apart in the entity-type list and counts in "lying in any" (adopted by Joe on 2026-11-19, D-111)). It is the same rule and the same assignment as C0 to C2, which is not independent validation. U1 to U3 need a cumulative-MW treatment on the inventory's site-year load (reconciliation_treatment.cumulative_mw, mw_source 'site_year_load'). The ownership classes are reconciliation_mu.adopted_row_u_ownership_classes(q), on quantities that cover 2001 to 2025 (a subset of years is refused in words). Each utility-state's class comes from the panel's entity type, the utility-level modal reported type carried across the panel to every year and state of the utility, and not the latest year-by-year EIA classification (D-119), read as the last nonmissing value of the panel's entity_type column over 2001 to 2025 (D-117), which on this panel returns that same type for every utility-state; the years searched are the quantity panel's 2001 to 2025, and the class is time-invariant, mapped by reconciliation_mu.U_MAP unchanged, settled by Joe on 2026-11-20 (D-117), the type described as his ruling of the same day states (D-119) (reconciliation_mu.OWNERSHIP_SPECIFICATION_D117). A utility-state with no entity type in any year searched gets no class. Under row U it leaves the sample, as a utility not reporting ownership-type data (Ryu and Hiatt p. 6). Under row C it is absent from the mapping, and ownership_split stops in words. A missing type is never read as any ownership class. The panel's entity_type is one type per utility id, the type its own filings report most often, so on this panel the reading over the years searched changes no class. Joe ruled on 2026-11-20 (D-119) that rows U and C keep this type, described as the utility-level modal reported type carried across the panel and not the latest year-by-year EIA classification, with no further raw-data investigation (his words are reconciliation_mu.OWNERSHIP_RULING_D119_WORDS); no claim is made that it equals EIA's year-by-year record (reconciliation_mu.PANEL_ENTITY_TYPE_STATEMENT). labels: Sensitivity scenario A, runner-up placement (Joe, D-107; R2 of D-106): every unresolved load-carrying site moved to the first other candidate that can hold its full load under the inventory's own placement rule, every date, capacity and basis as the inventory has it, each state's factor recomputed. Under Joe's rule (D-111) for what a candidate already carries, the 460 unresolved sites are lifted first, all other load kept counted, and placed in descending size, each counting where it lands; matching the earlier count is not the reason for the rule. Umatilla enters at 25.0 and 50.0 points at the caps (462 uncapped) and Portland General at 18.8 points. Besides its own kind of question it differs from the primary run in three ways: the two sites with no load history carry load at the early end of each of their questions (bi:852-0 from 2024; bi:837-0's date and the rest of its capacity at 2011), where the primary run leaves out every utility they reach; Oregon's factor is recomputed with those sites carrying load; and its sample differs (Portland General and Umatilla enter at the dose this history gives them, and any unit with load in this history and no 2009-2011 base leaves). It is a sensitivity scenario, not a bound and not necessarily a one-change comparison with the primary analysis.
not calibrated by the inference comparison

entries.reason: Out of scope for this freeze by Joe's ruling of 2026-11-19 (D-109). M0 to M4 are not run. The reasons, as they are: the row's sample flags and M0's assignment need inputs that are not read and not authorized (EIA-861 inputs under data/raw, the service-territory table, a site-to-county table and county boundaries); several elements of the paper's specification would be approximations of ours that Joe has not adopted; and he decided not to adopt them, not to read the additional tables and not to fetch county boundaries for this freeze. The row's code and tests are kept as they are and are dormant (run_outcomes._row_mu('M') as ROW_M_DORMANT_RUNNER, RowMInputs and NEEDS_M, and reconciliation_mu's row M parts); its verdict logic is dormant and not applied in this freeze, and no row M result supports a reproduction verdict. The paper's published numbers are reported as the paper's, as context, and nothing of ours is set beside them as a test. A utility or county with no territory row, no assigned site or no polygon is never described as untreated or as evidence of no treatment. Row M is in no executable order of unblinding and in no built count, and run() refuses it in words.
entries.context_reported_as_the_papers: The paper's published residential estimates, reported as the paper's and as context, with nothing of ours set beside them as a test (Meeks, Pless, Qi and Wang, 'Who Pays for Growth? Evidence from Data Centers and the Grid', SSRN 6967558, dated 2026-10-23; pooled, Table 2 col. 2, p. 47; investor-owned, public and cooperative, Table 3 Panels A to C col. 2, p. 48; standard errors in parentheses): pooled 0.021 (0.008), investor-owned 0.052 (0.014), public 0.017 (0.015), cooperative -0.007 (0.010).
